title: Vijayanagara Art and Architecture

cards.b: Vijayanagara (1336 to 1565) created a distinctive style at Hampi and in Andhra and Tamil Nadu. Questions ask about Hampi monuments, temple features, Krishnadevaraya’s patronage, gopurams and musical pillars. Hampi is a World Heritage Site (1986).

Hampi on the Tungabhadra (Karnataka) has two parts: the sacred centre (Virupaksha, Vitthala, Hemakuta) and the royal centre (Lotus Mahal, elephant stables, Mahanavami Dibba, Queen’s bath). Foreign travellers Domingo Paes and Abdur Razzak praised its size and wealth.

Virupaksha (Pampapati, Shiva), Vitthala temple (c. 16th century, stone chariot, musical pillars), Hazara Rama temple (a thousand Ramayana panels), Krishna temple built by Krishnadevaraya in 1515, Achyutaraya temple, giant monolithic Narasimha and Ganesha. Veerabhadra at Lepakshi (Andhra).

Blended Dravida with Deccani Islamic style. Features: tall raya gopurams (Krishnadevaraya’s gateways at Kalahasti, Kanchi, Chidambaram, Tiruvannamalai), kalyana mandapas (marriage halls with composite pillars), amman shrines for goddess, pillared corridors, horse-rearing pillars with rearing yalis, and Indo-Islamic arches in secular buildings like the Lotus Mahal.

Large bas-reliefs and dwarapalas, yali pillars, Bhakti-themed bronzes (Krishnadevaraya and his queens, Tirumala). Lepakshi murals in the Veerabhadra temple are major Vijayanagara paintings. Dance and music were patronised, and Telugu literature flourished (Krishnadevaraya’s Amuktamalyada, the Ashtadiggajas).

Hampi’s canals, stepped tanks and aqueducts were fed from the Tungabhadra by anicuts (Turtha canal). Fortification walls and gates enclosed the city in seven lines (Paes). Defeat at Talikota (1565) led to its sack, leaving the present ruins.

George Michell and others note Deccani influence in secular buildings, while temples stay Dravidian. Some argue Vijayanagara’s architecture is pure “Hindu empire”; others see it as a composite culture. “Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire” (1900) popularised the site.

Hampi (Group of Monuments at Hampi, UNESCO 1986) draws tourists; the Hampi Utsav and the Vijayanagara empire’s 650th-year events recall it. ASI and the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority protect it. Lepakshi (Andhra) is on the tentative list; the Basavanna bull is a major attraction.

• “Vijayanagara temple architecture and Dravida synthesis.”
  • Prelims: Vitthala temple, Hazara Rama, Lotus Mahal, Lepakshi.
  • Mains: Evaluate Krishnadevaraya as patron of art and literature.
